architecture: Independent feed-forward actor and critic; 58 inputs, no LSTM

inputs.history: Public choices within this game only. Count each decision to roll once, including before a bust. No inferred banking time. Counters follow player identity through rank sorting. Reset at new game.

probabilities.largeTargets: Existing rigorous lower and upper bounds. Both returned to network; not silently presented as exact.
probabilities.meaning: Probability that pot reaches a fixed strict-lead target before bust, not probability of winning.
probabilities.opponentPolicies: Original exact/bounded probability functions and two-roll search unchanged.
probabilities.catchUp: min over active opponents of ownScore+pot-opponentScore, with equality counting as a catch. Use one shared-pot hitting probability: exact through16384, lower/upper beyond. No active opponent returns0; already reachable returns1. Not a probability of losing or a forecast of opponent actions.

training.optimizer: Unchanged constant-rate Adam beta1 .9 beta2 .999 epsilon1e-8; no decay, warmup, gradient clipping or KL stop/rollback guard
training.syntheticStarts: 10%, no invented history; safe-phase starting pot marked unknown
training.memory: Feed-forward public history summaries; no recurrent state or sequence training

benchmarks.scripts: bankbench-46, unchanged fixtures and opponent behavior; older checkpoints imported as comparison references
benchmarks.challenge: bankbench-challenge-6, same equal regular mix, one follower every12 games, max two/type and max one follower
benchmarks.retention: Existing paired/fresh best-model validation, no automatic training rewinds

compatibility: 56-input compact checkpoints upgrade automatically, zero-inserting both feature weights and Adam moments in actor/critic input layers. Preserve all prior outputs, counters, optimizer step, champions and reports. Old save slots untouched. Earlier88-input models remain comparison references.
runtime: Offline JS Float32 Web Workers, 2–12 players, 10/15/20 rounds
claims: Functional validation only. No evidence yet that compact inputs improve playing strength.
